articles.title: Chenab river water level rises in J&K’s Reasi as Salal Dam opens 4 gates
articles.description: The Chenab river's water level rose in Reasi district on Tuesday. Authorities opened four gates of the Salal Dam to manage increased reservoir inflow. This action followed continuous rainfall in the upper catchment areas of the region. Water is now being released downstream in a controlled and regulated manner. Officials are closely monitoring the reservoir's water level and inflow conditions.

articles.title: 100-year-old Hindu temple demolished in Pakistan’s Punjab
articles.description: A historic Hindu temple in Pakistan's Punjab province was demolished on August 21. Minority groups allege religious zealots targeted the site for adjacent madrassa land. Local Hindu leaders express fear and call for government action against perpetrators.

articles.description: Brazil’s humpback whale population has recovered from about 2,000 to nearly 35,000 after commercial whaling pushed the species close to extinction. articles.title: Stock Market Live Updates Today: Markets open flat: Sensex down 19 points, Nifty at 24,078
articles.full_text: The S&P/TSX Composite Index fell 0.8% to 36,270.48 on August 31, its lowest close since August 6, as investors took profits ahead of a seasonally weak September. Despite the decline, the index gained nearly 3% in August, marking its fifth consecutive monthly advance. Materials fell 1.7% as gold prices hovered near a two-week low, while industrials and technology stocks dropped 1.3% each. Financials also declined 0.7%. Energy was among only two sectors to gain, rising 1.4% as oil prices jumped 2.8% to $85.76 a barrel following renewed US-Iran military action. Investor caution was also fuelled by a hawkish tone from the US Federal Reserve and expectations that the Bank of Canada will keep its benchmark rate unchanged at 2.25% on Wednesday. Indian shares are expected to open marginally higher on September 1 after data showed the economy grew a stronger-than-expected 7.8% year-on-year in the April-June quarter, helped by robust investment, manufacturing and consumer demand. GIFT Nifty futures pointed to a positive start for the Nifty 50, which closed at a one-month low of 24,080.4 on August 31. However, rising crude oil prices amid renewed Middle East tensions could limit gains. Brent crude rose to around $91 a barrel after fresh US-Iran attacks, while global bond yields climbed to new highs. The Nifty fell 1.2% in August as geopolitical concerns weighed on sentiment. Foreign investors also sold Indian shares worth Rs 79.86 billion on August 31. Markets will also track the weekly expiry of Nifty 50 derivatives, with a new closing auction mechanism expected to contribute to sharper swings in stocks and options. Among stocks to watch, ITC said its IT arm will acquire a 22.1% stake in Happiest Minds for about Rs 13.3 billion. ONGC plans to invest Rs 1 trillion over five years in deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration, while newly listed Milky Mist Dairy Food reported a sharp rise in April-June profit and a 43.6% increase in revenue. Shein shares fell about 10% in early trading in Hong Kong on September 1, as the online fashion retailer finally made its long-awaited stock market debut after years of efforts to go public. The shares opened at HK$48.56, matching the IPO price, before sliding to HK$43.80. The $1.7 billion offering valued Shein at $26.5 billion, far below its peak valuation of nearly $100 billion in 2022. Investor demand was relatively subdued, with the retail portion subscribed 5.63 times and the international tranche 2.59 times. Only about 6.6% of Shein's enlarged share capital was offered, while cornerstone investors took roughly one-fifth of the IPO. Shein's ultra-cheap fast-fashion model has come under pressure from higher tariffs, customs duties and regulatory scrutiny in the US and Europe. The US ended the de minimis duty exemption for low-value e-commerce shipments last year, while the EU has also moved to impose fees on such packages. The company swung to a net loss in the first quarter after annual net income fell 39% last year. Shein is now seeking to diversify beyond its own-label fashion business by expanding its third-party marketplace and offering supply-chain services to other brands. The Hong Kong IPO also allows Shein to make cash payments of about $3.5 billion and adjust shares for some early preferred investors who had invested at much higher valuations. Japan's Nikkei share average edged lower on September 1 as investors rotated out of technology stocks, while rising government bond yields weighed on risk sentiment. The tech-heavy Nikkei was down 0.2% at 66,173.86 after moving between gains and losses in early trading. In contrast, the broader Topix gained 0.5% to 4,178.62. AI-related stocks were among the biggest drags. Tokyo Electron fell 3.4% and Advantest declined 1.6%, while data-centre-linked cable makers Furukawa Electric and Fujikura dropped 4.9% and 3.9%, respectively. Silicon maker Sumco fell 4.1%. Japanese and US government bond yields climbed to fresh highs, with elevated oil prices and uncertainty in the Middle East adding to expectations of tighter monetary policy from the Bank of Japan and the Federal Reserve. Auto stocks benefited from the sector rotation, with Toyota and Nissan each rising 3.1%. Tokyo Electric Power Company was the Nikkei's biggest percentage gainer, up 5.1%.
